summary: Philip Stanley Rawson (1924–1995) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Winchester College, the University of Oxford, Courtauld Institute of Art (~1951–1953), and SOAS. He taught at the Royal College of Art and was Dean at the University of London (~1981–1984).

Philip Whalen (1923–2002) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned a BA at Reed College (~1946–1951) and studied under Richard Baker in 1972. He held posts at Naropa University, South Ridge Zendo, Dharma Sangha, and Hartford Street Zen Center.

Philipp André Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Bonn (1997–2004) under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. His posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and University of Leipzig (2016–2026).

Philipp Keiper (1855–1927) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1873–1877) under Friedrich von Spiegel and served as a Gymnasium teacher at Erlangen, Ludwigshafen, and Herzog-Wolfgang-Gymnasium.
Philipp Schäffer (1894–1943) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University between 1920 and 1924 under the supervision of Max Walleser.

Philippe Colinet (1853–1917) was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ghent, KU Leuven (Ph.D. 1881–1884 under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin), Berlin, and Paris. He later served as professor at KU Leuven from 1887.

Philippe Stern (1895–1979) was an art historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied under Louis Finot (~1920–1925). He served at the Guimet Museum (1921–1929; Conservateur-en-chef 1954–1965) and as professor of Indian art and archaeology at École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships in Tibetan at INALCO from 1842 and in Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1857 to 1894.
Phillip Bloom is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Philoxène Luzzatto (1829–1854) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Samuel David Luzzatto. He was a member of the Accademia Galileiana and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1852–1854).
Phra Athiwat Thammawatsiri specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he also serves as a lecturer and researcher.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat, and President of both the International Council for the Day of Vesak and the International Association of Buddhist Universities.

Phra Rajavaramuni specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned B.A. degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, later serving as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a Master of Buddhist Studies (2009) and a PhD (2015) at the University of Sydney, and held a post at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 2017.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni and completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle.
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held research appointments in 2015 at Ryukoku University and at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a B.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff (born 1947) is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her Ph.D. at Harvard (~1969–1973) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (2004).
